rows.question: Q1
rows.title: Welcome back (magic link primary)
rows.take: Magic link is the primary CTA, password is a secondary text link, SSO is a separate block: a clear hierarchy that makes passwords the exception.

rows.question: Q1
rows.title: Admin login settings: SSO, provisioning, domain control
rows.take: Single "Login" admin page with tabs for SSO, user provisioning and domain control — identity settings in one place.

rows.question: Q1
rows.title: Passwordless login to Analytics
rows.take: Email-only sign-in that doubles as sign-up; "check your email" step offers mail-client shortcuts and an explicit "Logging in…" state.

rows.question: Q1
rows.title: Sharing a doc
rows.take: An email can be granted 'Can edit' before the person exists; a 'Hasn't signed up' badge holds the seat until they arrive. Pattern for attaching a learner to a recording pre-account.

rows.question: Q1
rows.title: Email Login to Inbox
rows.take: Six-step magic-link login with distinct "sending link" and "link sent" states — the minimum viable passwordless loop.

rows.question: Q1
rows.title: Accepting invite
rows.take: COUNTER-EXAMPLE: 'Accept invite to view' still forces full name plus a 12-char password with 5 complexity rules, for a viewer-only invite. This is the friction that produces lockouts.

rows.question: Q1
rows.title: Developer account sign-up and magic-link login
rows.take: One email form serves both sign-up and log-in via magic link; in-app "Verify your log-in" confirmation before landing in the dashboard.

rows.question: Q1
rows.title: Email Magic-Link Onboarding
rows.take: Marketing CTA → auth-method card → email → link sent → empty team workspace; nothing asked beyond an email.

rows.question: Q1
rows.title: Team login policy: none / 2FA or SSO / SSO
rows.take: Three-radio login policy (none / 2FA or SSO / SSO only) with consequence text — org-level enforcement in one control.

rows.question: Q1
rows.title: Accepting an invite
rows.take: Invite email is already known, so 'Log in' sends a temporary magic link and drops the invitee straight into the team; no password is ever set up.

rows.question: Q1
rows.title: Logging in
rows.take: One login screen offers Google, email magic link, SAML SSO and passkey as peers; the 'check your email' step has an 'enter code manually' fallback for when links don't open.

rows.question: Q1
rows.title: Sign in to Miro
rows.take: 'Trouble signing in? Request a magic sign-in link' as the recovery path next to reset-password, and 'sign in to a private organization' for SSO tenants; answers the months-long lockout problem.

rows.question: Q1
rows.title: Continue as a visitor
rows.take: Visitor mode: a shared board asks only for a display name and lets the person in; the closest analogue to attaching a learner to a recording without an account.

rows.question: Q1
rows.title: Passwordless sign-in & Organization Setup
rows.take: "Sign in with work email" magic link lands straight in org creation — identity first, workspace second, no password anywhere.

rows.question: Q1
rows.title: Continue with email (sign in or create)
rows.take: 'We'll sign you in or create an account if you don't have one yet': one entry point collapses login and signup so the invitee never has to know which they need.

rows.question: Q1
rows.title: Logging in
rows.take: Email first, then 'Continue with SSO', then a 'Select an organization' picker: identity comes from the org's IdP and the user just chooses which tenant to enter.

rows.question: Q1
rows.title: Logging In
rows.take: Magic-link login end to end, including the email itself: link expires in 20 min, single use, plus a copyable URL for signing in on a different device.

rows.question: Q1
rows.title: Accepting an invite
rows.take: COUNTER-EXAMPLE: invite acceptance is a plain signup form (name + password) with the email pre-filled; the invite context buys nothing beyond the headline.

rows.question: Q1
rows.title: SSO authentication settings (admin)
rows.take: Org SSO settings page: "no providers yet" empty state with one "Manage integrations" CTA — SSO as an admin toggle, invisible to end users.

rows.question: Q1
rows.title: Sign into workspace
rows.take: Domain auto-join ('if you have an @school.edu address you can join this organization') plus a 'Send magic link' vs 'Type password' choice on the same email field.

rows.question: Q1
rows.title: Accepting an invitation
rows.take: Three parallel ways in: a shareable join link ('anyone with this link can join'), import from Google/Slack contacts (roster source), or typed emails. Roster-import is the Canvas analogue.

rows.question: Q2
rows.title: Set access (document)
rows.take: Attribute-scoped access on a document: Workplace x Department x Role dropdowns instead of naming people; maps to site x program x cohort for a sim center.

rows.question: Q2
rows.title: Sharing a project
rows.take: Project-level 'Access settings' switch (My workspace vs Private to members) sits above a member list where each row carries its own role (Project admin / Editor / Viewer).

rows.question: Q2
rows.title: Request access to project
rows.take: Denied state that routes to the project's admins (not a global admin) with an optional message for the approver; scoped access needs a scoped request path.

rows.question: Q2
rows.title: What can Jane Doe access?
rows.take: Person-centric inverse of the share dialog: a checklist of projects one person may see, with a plain-English 'what happens next'. Direct answer to 'faculty sees only their own students'.

rows.question: Q2
rows.title: Share modal controls
rows.take: One share modal combines link-access dropdown, collaborator invite, and per-collaborator role change/remove.

rows.question: Q2
rows.title: Folder sharing management
rows.take: Share a document folder to a specific shareholder or group from the folder context menu — you pick a person/group, not a global role.

rows.question: Q2
rows.title: Project sharing & link invite
rows.take: Video-project share menu: send link to recipients (autosuggest) plus separate link settings; includes share error and retry states.

rows.question: Q2
rows.title: Hub permissions (per-user grid)
rows.take: COUNTER-EXAMPLE: per-user grid of 15 checkbox columns (view, delete own, add, archive, export...) with Users/Groups/Guests tabs; granular but unreadable, and per space rather than per content.

rows.question: Q2
rows.title: Folder access management
rows.take: Folder "Manage access" dialog with a per-collaborator permission selector and inline confirmation of the change.

rows.question: Q2
rows.title: Sharing a project
rows.take: Splits the audience into Collaborators vs Readers tabs, then stacks three scopes with their own level: named people, Workspace Access, Public Access.

rows.question: Q2
rows.title: Manage sharing and invite collaborator
rows.take: Per-file share settings switch link access to "Only invited people", then invite by email — item-level scope overrides team default.

rows.question: Q2
rows.title: Team (User Groups)
rows.take: Recording tool that sells user groups explicitly as 'easily share meetings with a particular group': groups exist to receive recordings, not to hold a global role.

rows.question: Q2
rows.title: Repository roles
rows.take: Five pre-defined roles, each described in one sentence as 'previous role plus X', applied per repository via teams; custom roles are an escape hatch, not the default.

rows.question: Q2
rows.title: Invite client to workspace
rows.take: External-client invite modal lets you adjust what the client can see before sending; pending invite shown in the client list.

rows.question: Q2
rows.title: Sharing a project
rows.take: One input for 'users, groups, or collections'; the whole-workspace row is a toggle with its own level; and a 'prevent Can-edit users from re-sharing' checkbox stops privilege leaking.

rows.question: Q2
rows.title: Share reel: team-only vs anyone with link
rows.take: Two radios — "Only members in your team" vs "Anyone with the link" — the minimal audience choice for sharing a recording.

rows.question: Q2
rows.title: Creating a group
rows.take: People table with Teamspaces / Groups / Role as separate columns, and a Groups tab that shows how many teamspaces each group unlocks; groups are a sharing target, role stays minimal.

rows.question: Q2
rows.title: Share a document
rows.take: Share dialog is organised by audience tab: Workspace Members (Restricted) / Guests / Everyone (No Access). Being in the workspace does not mean seeing the document.

rows.question: Q2
rows.title: Share document: invite with role + public link toggle
rows.take: Doc-level modal: invite by email with role, list of guests vs team members, and a public-link toggle — all scoped to one document.

rows.question: Q2
rows.title: Roles permission matrix
rows.take: COUNTER-EXAMPLE: global capability x role checkbox matrix (dozens of rows, 'Add Role' button). This is the 8-global-roles trap: it can never express 'only my students' videos'.

rows.question: Q2
rows.title: Invite External Collaborator
rows.take: Guest invited to a single project: a "Review external access" step warns what they will see, then a permission level is chosen.

rows.question: Q2
rows.title: Community Access Management
rows.take: Gate a content area by audience: pick which membership tiers can access the community in a modal — edtech cohort-based scoping.

rows.question: Q2
rows.title: Share Video project
rows.take: Video-specific share: 'All admins - Can manage' as an implicit row, owner, named person with Can comment, and a separate Link privacy control; Collaborators vs Viewers counted in the comments panel.

rows.question: Q3
rows.title: Client Import/Export
rows.take: CSV import with a "mapping required" preview state and column labels applied before a success banner on the client list.

rows.question: Q3
rows.title: Bulk Stakeholder Import
rows.take: Auto-maps columns on upload, then validates on import attempt with row-level errors before committing.

rows.question: Q3
rows.title: Admin center: Groups
rows.take: Admin "Groups" area organizes members by department/location with group admins — cohort structure with delegated admin.

rows.question: Q3
rows.title: Manage team members
rows.take: Multi-select people in the roster → "Add to group" overlay — groups/cohorts built from the existing member list.

rows.question: Q3
rows.title: SSO & provisioning: domain verification
rows.take: "SSO & provisioning" settings with domain-verification tab — directory sync is set up next to SSO, not as a separate product.

rows.question: Q3
rows.title: Importing members
rows.take: 'Enter manually | Import CSV' is a toggle inside the same Invite wizard (not a buried settings page), with a template CSV link and tag assignment for the whole batch; answers the 'batch upload existed but nobody found it' problem.

rows.question: Q3
rows.title: Importing member from CSV
rows.take: Bulk import page shows the invite email preview and defaults before upload, then a 'Bulk logs' table (Pending -> Completed 2/2, input + output CSV) so a tech can verify what actually landed.

rows.question: Q3
rows.title: Mapping fields
rows.take: 3-step Upload / Map fields / Review; the review screen counts new vs existing people, warnings and errors, and offers 'add these people to a new or existing segment' — i.e. import creates the cohort in one go.

rows.question: Q3
rows.title: Uploading a CSV (bulk edit of workers)
rows.take: COUNTER-EXAMPLE: download-edit-upload-validate-choose-review, a 4-stage wizard in a full-screen takeover; right for 300 payroll records, far too heavy for a sim tech adding a 4-10 learner group.

rows.question: Q3
rows.title: Admin console: Members list with status filter
rows.take: Admin members table with status filter (invited/active) and Groups as a sibling nav item — roster + cohorts in one console.

rows.question: Q3
rows.title: Creating a teammate group
rows.take: Create-group form offers both a checkbox picker of existing people AND 'Download CSV template / Import CSV' inline — small groups by hand, big cohorts by file, same screen.

rows.question: Q3
rows.title: Importing members
rows.take: CSV import as column-mapping table (field / sample data / import as), upserts on matching email, and auto-labels the batch 'Import <date>' so the cohort is findable afterwards.

rows.question: Q3
rows.title: Manage members
rows.take: Group page puts Add members / Bulk upload members / Download members side by side, and separates direct vs indirect (nested) members — a model for cohorts that contain sub-groups.

rows.question: Q3
rows.title: Invite members dialog (link, email, 'Import list' nudge)
rows.take: Invite dialog surfaces bulk import as a one-line nudge under the email box ('Want to add emails in bulk? Import list') plus a domain-restricted join link — discoverability of bulk without a separate feature.

rows.question: Q3
rows.title: CSV User Import
rows.take: Import wizard maps each CSV column to a user attribute, then ends with a post-import report of created/updated/failed rows.

rows.question: Q3
rows.title: Inviting team members
rows.take: Paste comma-separated emails + optional 'Add to team' in one dialog; invitees appear immediately in the members table with '(Invited)' status and their team chip, so the roster exists before anyone accepts.

rows.question: Q3
rows.title: Invite to team: paste multiple emails
rows.take: Multiline paste box for bulk emails with an "add individually" fallback — one field handles 1 or 100 invites.

rows.question: Q3
rows.title: Import contacts from CSV
rows.take: Canonical CSV import: upload → map columns (auto then manual) → review parsed rows → importing indicator → list.

rows.question: Q3
rows.title: Invite teammates (link, Google/Slack contacts, emails)
rows.take: Three entry paths stacked on one card: join link, pull from Google/Slack contacts, or type emails — a join link/code is the cheapest answer to a cohort that churns until week one (learners self-enrol).

rows.question: Q3
rows.title: Add and enroll student
rows.take: Add students manually with an "enroll in course" toggle in the same modal, then import feedback and an updated roster.

rows.question: Q3
rows.title: Invite people to meal plan
rows.take: Same invite modal supports manual emails or CSV upload; shows format error and an "imported 0 of 5" review list to fix rows.

rows.question: Q3
rows.title: Event registrants list with 'Sync from email list' and 'Upload CSV'
rows.take: Roster header offers 'Sync from email list' next to 'Upload CSV' with an in-page progress toast; sync (continuous, from a source of truth) and upload (one-off) are distinct verbs, matching SIS/Canvas vs spreadsheet.

rows.question: Q4
rows.title: Manage team member permission
rows.take: Change a member's permission from the row via a selector and confirm inline — no edit page.

rows.question: Q4
rows.title: Workspace Guest Invitation
rows.take: Separate "Guests" area for external people with a restricted role — guest as a first-class, clearly bounded role.

rows.question: Q4
rows.title: Updating sharing permissions
rows.take: Share dialog stacks audience rows — anyone with link / anyone in workspace / inherited from folder (greyed) / named people — each with Can view / comment / edit / No access; inherited rows are shown but locked.

rows.question: Q4
rows.title: Invite Users from Platform Settings
rows.take: Role dropdown plus a "Roles help" explainer inside the invite modal; pending invites list updates in place.

rows.question: Q4
rows.title: Project Access Management
rows.take: Per-project collaborator roles override the workspace role — the per-item escape hatch next to a small global role set.

rows.question: Q4
rows.title: Editing member role
rows.take: Three roles (Employee / Auditor / Admin) as a segmented control with the selected role's description underneath; members table also has 'Import from spreadsheet' and a join link right in the header.

rows.question: Q4
rows.title: Team permissions matrix (Basic / Low / Med / High / Owner)
rows.take: COUNTER-EXAMPLE: permission levels named Basic/Low/Med/High carry no meaning — the admin must read the whole grid to know what 'Med' does; role names should describe a job, not a rank.

rows.question: Q4
rows.title: Changing a member role
rows.take: The floor: exactly two roles (Admin / Member), each with a one-line description in the dropdown, 'Remove from workspace' as the third option; role changes are a single click with a toast, no confirm.

rows.question: Q4
rows.title: Share space with 'Inherited' org access and explicit per-person role
rows.take: Labels the org-wide row as 'Inherited' with member count while a named person has an explicit 'Administrator' override, plus a toggle to mint a guest link with its own role — three layers, one small panel.

rows.question: Q4
rows.title: Changing a role
rows.take: Users page is split into Invited / Guests / Members sections; a role cell offers 'Convert to guest' / 'Convert to admin' / 'Remove' with a lightweight inline confirm — guest is a conversion, not a separate account type.

rows.question: Q4
rows.title: Inviting a guest
rows.take: Per-item escape hatch on top of workspace roles: Share panel lists people (with 'Guest' badge), the teamspace, and 'General access: Everyone at <workspace>', each with its own Full access / Can edit / Can comment level.

rows.question: Q4
rows.title: Invite member with Guest / Member / Admin / Owner dropdown
rows.take: The canonical 4-role ladder with descriptions inline at invite time: Guest 'only projects they're invited to', Member 'create and access projects', Admin 'manage members and settings', Owner 'billing and transfer'.

rows.question: Q4
rows.title: Add and assign employee permissions
rows.take: COUNTER: role choice, then per-business, then per-permission checklist — 8 steps to add one employee; matrix explosion.

rows.question: Q4
rows.title: Adding a new role
rows.take: Roles as cards with plain-language descriptions and head counts, plus a dashed 'Add new role' card as the escape hatch; custom role permissions are grouped by AREA with just View / Edit columns, not per-action toggles.

rows.question: Q4
rows.title: Invite Members
rows.take: Invite modal with an expandable "view role descriptions" panel so people pick the right role without leaving the flow.

rows.question: Q4
rows.title: Permission groups (apps x resources x users)
rows.take: COUNTER: "Permission groups" each tracking apps × resources × users — admin must reason about a 3-D matrix to answer "who can see X".

rows.question: Q4
rows.title: Inviting people (guest)
rows.take: Switching 'Invite as' to Guest progressively reveals required channels + an expiration date; a guest is scoped to content and time — the pattern for simulated patients or visiting faculty without a dedicated global role.

rows.question: Q4
rows.title: Adding a role
rows.take: COUNTER-EXAMPLE: roles x permissions checkbox matrix that gains a column per role and a row per action; adding 'Contributor' means auditing ~30 cells. This is what 8 global roles turns into.

rows.question: Q4
rows.title: Team Member Invitation and Role Assignment
rows.take: Role chosen at invite time from a short fixed list with one-line descriptions — no separate role-admin step.

rows.question: Q4
rows.title: Workspace members: Members / Guests tabs
rows.take: Members vs Guests tabs; each row shows role and license — guest is a tab, not a role-matrix column.

rows.question: Q4
rows.title: User Roles with View permissions
rows.take: Fixed role list (Primary Owner / Owner / Author / Affiliate) with a "View permissions" expander — small set, fully transparent.

rows.question: Q4
rows.title: Downgrading a member
rows.take: Member -> Guest downgrade opens a confirm that spells out the consequences ('can only access channels they've been invited to, can't invite members') with an explicit 'Yes, I'm absolutely sure' checkbox.

rows.question: Q4
rows.title: Team member roles and access
rows.take: Per-member "roles and access" page: one role plus product-level access toggles — the escape hatch lives on the person, not in a matrix.

rows.question: Q5
rows.title: Track share and invite link
rows.take: Track sharing: invite-only vs public, allow downloads, password-protect — media-specific link controls in one panel.

rows.question: Q5
rows.title: Manage track share link
rows.take: Reset share link with a confirmation dialog — old link dies, new one issued; the simplest revoke pattern.

rows.question: Q5
rows.title: Share item link: expires after + available to
rows.take: "Link expires after" + "Available to" (anyone / specific emails) — two dropdowns cover expiry and audience for a shared item.

rows.question: Q5
rows.title: View-only link panel
rows.take: View-only link explicitly framed as 'allows anyone to see the file, no sign-in required', with a LIVE badge, preview of what recipients will see, password toggle and Delete link / Update link.

rows.question: Q5
rows.title: Share link to board - settings
rows.take: Security tier for media links: 'Require name and email to view' (lightweight identification without an account), passcode, expiration date - each an independent toggle.

rows.question: Q5
rows.title: Share Base Public Link
rows.take: Public link lives on its own "Share publicly" tab, configured separately from collaborator invites.

rows.question: Q5
rows.title: Share link and set permission
rows.take: Switch from restricted to link-based access and choose the link's permission level in the same step, then copy.

rows.question: Q5
rows.title: Generating a share link
rows.take: COUNTER-EXAMPLE (with one keeper): per-field permission checklist and 1-hour default expiry are overkill for training content, but the live '59 mins' countdown ring on the published-link screen is a good way to make a time-box visible.

rows.question: Q5
rows.title: Adding expiration date
rows.take: Publish-to-web popover lists Password / Email access / Expiration as one stack of settings with 'Never' defaults; calendar offers 'Expire on Thu, Apr 30' vs 'Never expires'; a single Unpublish button revokes, and a viewer count shows who actually used the link.

rows.question: Q5
rows.title: Editing share settings
rows.take: Separate 'Link for editing' vs 'Link for viewing' tabs, each with its own expiration toggle+date, password and download controls; 'Restrictions apply - Modify' surfaces the constraint next to Copy link; 'Unshare file' as the revoke-all action.

rows.question: Q5
rows.title: Share settings
rows.take: Link settings decomposed into three questions - Who can access / What can they do (View vs Edit) / Additional security - and a note that link settings do not override people already invited directly.

rows.question: Q5
rows.title: Create and schedule post
rows.take: Schedule a membership post's publication date/time from the post editor — scheduled publish for gated content.

rows.question: Q5
rows.title: Scheduling an expiration date
rows.take: Video share panel: expiry with quick presets (24h / 1 week / 2 weeks) plus exact date+time, passphrase toggle, and the resulting expiry shown inline as 'Dec 31 at 11:59pm' with Edit.

rows.question: Q5
rows.title: Scheduling a post
rows.take: Publish step as a plain-language sentence ('Set it live now' vs 'Schedule for later' + date/time), then a confirmation 'Your post will be published on October 25th at 01:42' with a one-click 'Unschedule and revert to draft' undo.

rows.question: Q5
rows.title: Invite link creation
rows.take: Admin-created invite link carries a role, a usage limit and an expiry date — cohort self-enrolment with a built-in shelf life.

rows.question: Q5
rows.title: Sharing settings - share the link with
rows.take: The OneDrive/SharePoint model the customer asked for: audience radio (Anyone / People you choose / People with existing access), then Can edit level, expiry date field, 'Require verification' and 'Set password' in one compact sheet.

rows.question: Q5
rows.title: Shareable Link Creation
rows.take: "Configure protections" step before the link is generated — expiry/password set up-front, not as an afterthought.

rows.question: Q5
rows.title: Updating link access
rows.take: 'Visitor link access' is a distinct tier for people WITHOUT an account (anonymous learners): its own view/no-access level, optional password, expiration date shown as 'Expires Feb 28, 2025, 10:50 AM GMT-7', and 'Reset visitor link' to revoke by rotating the URL without touching workspace members.

rows.question: Q5
rows.title: Sharing a file (NordLocker)
rows.take: COUNTER-EXAMPLE: terms checkbox before generating a link, a separate security code the sender must transmit out-of-band, fixed expiry you cannot change, link frozen to one file version - security that pushes work onto the sharer.

rows.question: Q5
rows.title: Proton Drive public link settings
rows.take: Revocation written as a consequence, not a verb: 'Stop sharing - erase this link and remove everyone with access', sitting under expiration date and link password toggles.

rows.question: Q5
rows.title: Edit shared link: permission + expires after
rows.take: Edit an existing per-recipient link: permission dropdown + "Expires after" — expiry remains editable after the link is created.

rows.question: Q5
rows.title: Updating content status
rows.take: Course lessons carry a Draft / Published / Scheduled / Public preview status badge with a date; multi-select lessons and 'Set status for 2 selected' in bulk - the closest analogue to faculty releasing recordings on a date.

rows.question: Q6
rows.title: Login & security: password, passkeys, sign out all
rows.take: Login & security page manages password and passkeys side by side, plus "sign out of all devices".

rows.question: Q6
rows.title: Logging in (email code, 'Last used' badge)
rows.take: A 'Last used' badge on the sign-in method you picked last time (email vs Google vs Microsoft) - removes the 'which account did I use?' guess that causes duplicate accounts and lockouts.

rows.question: Q6
rows.title: SSO email check and error handling
rows.take: Enter email → system checks for SSO config → clear error when the domain has no SSO — email-first routing.

rows.question: Q6
rows.title: Account recovery: recovery codes
rows.take: Account recovery page lists masked recovery codes with remove and "+ New recovery code" — recovery as a managed inventory.

rows.question: Q6
rows.title: Logging in (magic link)
rows.take: 'Sign in with email' as one of several login options; confirmation screen with 'Go to inbox' and an always-visible 'Back to login options' escape so a user never gets stuck on a method.

rows.question: Q6
rows.title: Sign-in to Content Home
rows.take: After email, choose "password or one-time code" — lets users skip password recall without a reset.

rows.question: Q6
rows.title: Password reset via one-time code
rows.take: Password reset via one-time code typed inline, no link to click — fewer context switches.

rows.question: Q6
rows.title: Logging In (email or Google, no password)
rows.take: Minimal 'plug and play' entry: one Google button and one email field - there is no password to forget, no sign-up vs sign-in split, and 'Check your inbox' offers only Resend.

rows.question: Q6
rows.title: Post-login prompt - add passkey
rows.take: 'Log in faster next time' banner shown right after a successful login - the moment to offer a passkey - with a dismiss X, never a blocking step.

rows.question: Q6
rows.title: Logging in (magic link)
rows.take: Work-email-only sign in, no password field exists; after sending the link it offers 'Open your email client: Gmail / Outlook / Superhuman' buttons to close the loop in one click.

rows.question: Q6
rows.title: SSO sign-in with team identifier
rows.take: SSO entry via team identifier with an explicit SSO-initiation error state.

rows.question: Q6
rows.title: Sign-in to Business Dashboard
rows.take: After password + 2FA, prompt passkey enrolment so the next login is one step.

rows.question: Q6
rows.title: Incorrect password - send a code instead
rows.take: Microsoft account (the institution's own IdP): wrong password shows 'Send a code to <email>' inline under Next - relevant because hospital/university users already live in this pattern.

rows.question: Q6
rows.title: Password recovery and reset
rows.take: Complete recovery loop: error → enter email → loading → "instructions sent" → set new password → back in.

rows.question: Q6
rows.title: Two-factor authentication setup
rows.take: 2FA setup shows recovery codes and requires acknowledgement before finishing — recovery set up when access is set up.

rows.question: Q6
rows.title: Resetting password (with one-time code escape hatch)
rows.take: On 'Incorrect email address or password' the same screen offers 'Log in with a one-time code' as an OR path, and the reset itself is a 6-digit emailed code rather than a link.

rows.question: Q6
rows.title: Resetting password
rows.take: COUNTER-EXAMPLE: vague 'Unable to verify your account' error, only exit is Forgot password -> emailed reset link -> new password -> log in again; the whole session depends on the recovery email working.

rows.question: Q6
rows.title: Email Code Sign-In
rows.take: On password mismatch, offer an email code instead of a reset link; handles invalid code and retry.

rows.question: Q6
rows.title: Recover Account - link invalid or expired
rows.take: COUNTER-EXAMPLE of the expired-link dead end: 'link you followed is invalid, or it has expired' with only a text 'try again' - shows why magic links need a code fallback and a visible expiry.

rows.question: Q6
rows.title: Security settings - passkey recommended, secondary email
rows.take: Security page ranks Passkeys 'Recommended' above Password, explains 'takes under a minute', and adds 'Secondary email - used to restore access' so recovery does not depend on one institutional mailbox.

rows.question: Q6
rows.title: Recover your account with recovery key
rows.take: COUNTER-EXAMPLE: recovery depends on a key PDF saved on 'the device you used to sign up' - exactly the hidden recovery dependency that produces six-month lockouts; failure message gives no alternative.

rows.question: Q6
rows.title: Too many login attempts - login with code
rows.take: Rate-limit dialog offers 'Login with code' as the primary way out instead of a hard lockout - the direct antidote to months-long password lockouts.

rows.question: Q6
rows.title: Logging in with passcode
rows.take: The 'forgot password' link is rewritten as 'Forgot password? Log in with passcode' - the recovery path IS a login path (emailed code), so a forgotten password never blocks the session or requires a reset.

rows.question: Q6
rows.title: Create a passkey
rows.take: Passkey modal explains in plain words what you will log in with (Face ID / Touch ID / Passcode); Security page also lists Recovery phone as a backup channel and current login activity.

rows.question: Q6
rows.title: Logging in (6-digit email code)
rows.take: One-time code instead of a link (works when the email client is on another device); 'Use a different email' and a yellow nudge 'still waiting on your code? try signing up instead' handle the no-account case without a dead end.

rows.question: Q6
rows.title: Sign in with Google / Microsoft / LinkedIn / SSO / instant link
rows.take: One screen offers every institutional path - Google, Microsoft, SSO - AND 'Email me a link to sign in instantly' as a peer of the password button, so a locked-out user has three ways in without support.
